source_text: μελλόντων ἢ αὐθεντείαν τοῦ χρηματίζειν, ὡς ὁ θεὸς ἔχειν δύνανται; εἰ δὲ οὐκ ἴσασι μὲν οὗτοι ἀφ' ἑαυτῶν οὐδὲ κατ' ἐξουσίαν ἰδίαν χρηματίζουσιν, ὡς ἔστι καὶ δίχα συστάσεώς τινος τὸ πρᾶγμα αὐταπόδεικτον, διὰ δὲ τὸ τὴν λέξιν μόνην κατὰ κοινοῦ κατηγορεῖσθαι ἐπὶ τὴν μέμψιν καὶ τὴν κατηγορίαν παρηγγείλατε, προπετῶς καὶ ἀδιασκέπτως ἐπράξατε, καὶ οὐδὲ πρὸς τὸ πρᾶγμα. οὐδὲ γὰρ εἰ τὸν θεὸν πατέρα φαῖεν τυχὸν ἄλλοι τινές, ὅτι χρηματίζει καὶ ἀγαθός ἐστιν, ἡμᾶς τὸ ἐναντίον λέγειν πρέπον. εἴπω τι ὑμῖν καὶ ἕτερον· «βλέπετε μὴ τὸν χρηματίσαντα τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ ἄγγελον, τὸν ἅγιον τῶν ἁγίων, σωτῆρα εἶπεν; τῷ γὰρ ὀνόματι τούτῳ προσχρησαμένῃ ἐπικεκρυμμένως σὺν ἐμφάσει πολλῇ καὶ θείᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ φαίνεται ἡ γραφὴ διὰ τὸ ἀγγεῖλαι ἐν τῇ οἰκονομίᾳ ὡς υἱὸν λόγον τὸ πατρικὸν βούλημα. οὐ γὰρ εἶπεν ὀνομαστί, ὡς εἴωθεν λέγειν· Μιχαήλ, Γαβριὴλ ἢ ὁ δεῖνα.» τί τοίνυν ἐξ ἁπάντων τῶν ἡμετέρων λόγων αἰτιάσαιτ' ἂν τίς εὐλόγως; τί δὲ μέμψαιτο τῇ οὐδαμόθεν ἐχούσῃ τὸ εὐθύνεσθαι ὀρθοδόξων πίστει; πῶς δὲ οὐ πιστεύειν ἄξιον, ὡς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα βασιλικῶς ἤτοι θεϊκῶς χρηματίζει, οἱ δ' ἄγγελοι λειτουργικῶς ἤγουν διακονικῶς; ὡς χαλεπὸν οὖν, καθά φησιν, οἰάκων ἔχεσθαι. ὅτῳ κυβερνητικῆς οὐχ ὕπεστιν, οὕτω χαλεπὸν καὶ διδάσκειν, ὅτῳ ἡ χάρις τοῦ θείου πνεύματος ἡ τῶν ἀνθρώπων σὺν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ ἐργαζομένη τὴν σωτηρίαν οὐ πάρεστιν, οὔτε ἐστὶν τὸ εἰδέναι τὴν καὶ ἐν τοῖς αἰνίγμασιν τῶν λογίων εὑρισκομένην ἀσφάλειαν καὶ τὴν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐπιστήμης τῶν πιστῶν ἀνδρῶν διδομένην ἀπόκρισιν, καὶ ὅτῳ ἐριστικῆς καὶ ἀντιλογικῆς καὶ ποικίλης προαιρέσεως ἄνευ οὐκ ἔστιν λόγου προφορά. οἶδα δὲ σαφῶς, ὦ εὐδόκιμοι καὶ τὸ οὐράνιον φῶς κατοικοῦντες ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅτιπερ ὑμεῖς ὡς ἄμεμπτοι καὶ τέλειοι οὐκ ἠχθέσθητε ἐπὶ τοῖς λεχθεῖσιν παρ' ἐμοῦ, ἕνεκα τῶν κατὰ τὴν φύσιν, οὐ κατὰ τὸ ἐπαινετὸν τῆς γνώμης, ὁμοίων ὑμῖν ἀγγέλων· οἷς ἐξ ἀρχῆς μέμψις παρηκολούθησεν, ὡς καὶ οἵτινες ὑμῖν μάλιστα ἀπίθανοί τινες πρὸς τὸν κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας ἀγῶνα φαίνονται. ὁ γὰρ λόγος μοί ἐστιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ θεϊκοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ φωτίζοντος ἅπαντα καὶ φιλοτιμουμένου τὰ θεϊκὰ τοῖς κτίσμασι τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ μονογενοῦς αὐτοῦ ἐφάμιλλα, τοῦ ἁγιάσαντος καὶ ὑμᾶς καὶ συνδοξαζομένου παρ' ὑμῶν ἅμα τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ διὰ τοῦ τρισαγίου αἴνου. μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ συνεπενεύσατε πνεῦμα τοῦτο τῆς ὑποστάσεως τοῦ θεοῦ ἓν καὶ μόνον καὶ θεὸν ἀνευφημήσαντί μοι· καὶ ἐβούλεσθε ἂν τάχα πανηγυρίζει δέ μοι ἐν τῷ μέρει τούτῳ τὸ βιβλίον δι' ὑπερβολὴν εὐνοίας ὑμῶν τῆς περὶ τὴν σεπτὴν καὶ ὁμοούσιον τριάδα ὑμετέρα τε εἶναι ῥήματα τὰ ἐκ τῆς τῶν γραφῶν διανοίας λεχθέντα παρὰ πολλῶν καὶ νῦν παρ' ἐμοῦ καὶ μηδέποτε σιωπὴν τούτοις ἐπιβληθῆναι, καὶ πάντας δὲ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τὴν ἀπὸ τῶν πραγμάτων σχολὴν δαπανᾶν εἰς ὑπόθεσιν τοιαύτην. τοιγαροῦν διὰ τοῦτο κρίσει τῇ ὑπερτάτῃ, σὺ μὲν, ὦ ἅγιε Μιχαήλ, ἄρχειν τῶν 76 ἀσωμάτων στρατιῶν προεχειρίσθης καὶ ζώνῃ οἷον νοερᾷ ἐτιμήθης, καὶ εὐωδία τις τῆς πάντων δεσποζούσης παναγοῦς καὶ οἰκτίρμονος τριάδος ὑπάρχεις· σὺ δέ, ὦ ἅγιε Γαβριήλ, διακονήσασθαι τῷ μυστηρίῳ τῆς ἀφράστου οἰκονομίας, ὡς ἐχέμυθος καὶ πιστός, ἐξελέγης· ἄλλος δὲ ἄλλῳ, οὐδὲ αἰτήσας, θεοσδότῳ χαρίσματι τετίμηται, οἵῳ μὴ καὶ ἕτεροι, καὶ οἵῳ μὴ καὶ ἡμεῖς· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡμεῖς, οἵῳ μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς. ὁ γὰρ θεὸς λόγος οὐ διὰ τοὺς ἁμαρτήσαντας ἀγγέλους ἄγγελος, ἀλλὰ διὰ τοὺς ἐν ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀνθρώπους ἄνθρωπος, ἀτρέπτως, ἀσυγχύτως, ἀναμαρτήτως, ἀφράστως, ὡς οἶδεν καὶ ἠβουλήθη, ἐκ τῆς παρθένου καὶ κατὰ τὴν σάρκα αὐτῆς καὶ πάντων ἡμῶν ἐγένετο, μείνας ὃ ἦν καὶ ἔστιν καὶ ἔσται, εἷς καὶ αὐτός. «εἷς γάρ», φησίν, «ἅγιος, εἷς κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς εἰς δό ξαν θεοῦ πατρός.» καὶ οὕτως, ὡς ἀπὸ γῆς εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀνέβη, ἥξει τὸ δεύτερον, διακονουμένων αὐτῷ ἀγγελικῶν εὐδοκίμων φαλάγγων μυρίων μυριάδων, καὶ ἔτι καὶ κρινεῖ καὶ ποιήσει κατὰ τὴν φιλανθρωπίαν αὐτοῦ. διὸ μετὰ τὰς ἐκκλησίας καὶ οἶκοι εὐκτήριοι τῷ θεῷ τῆς προσηγορίας ὑμῶν ἐπώνυμοι, ὦ εὐάρεστος ξυνωρὶς ἀρχαγγέλων, οὐκ ἐν μόναις ταῖς πόλεσιν, ἀλλὰ καὶ στενωποῖς ἰδίᾳ καὶ οἰκίαις καὶ ἀγροῖς ἱδρύνθησαν, χρυσῷ καὶ ἀργύρῳ ἢ καὶ ἐλέφαντι κοσμηθέντες· ἴασίν τε οἱ ἄνθρωποι καὶ εἰς τὰ ἀπωτέρω τῆς ἐνεγκαμένης αὐτοὺς χωρία τὰ ἔχοντα οἷον ὡς πρυτανεῖα ἐπιτευγμάτων τὰ εὐκτήρια προβεβλημένα, οὐκ ὀκνοῦντες καὶ πέλαγος διαλαβεῖν, ἢ δέοι, μακρόν, καὶ πολλῶν ἐφεξῆς ἡμερῶν ὁδὸν
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: 'For if God did not spare angels who sinned,' what innate knowledge of the] things to come or [what] authority of giving revelation can they have, as God? But if these neither know from themselves nor give revelation by their own authority, as the matter is self-evident even without some proof, but because the word alone is predicated in common you passed the word to blame and accusation, you acted rashly and without consideration, and not even toward the matter. For not even if some others perhaps should say of God the Father that he gives revelation and is good, [would it be] fitting for us to say the opposite. Let me say to you something else too: 'Look whether [Scripture] did not call the angel who gave revelation to the centurion, the Holy of the holies, Saviour; for Scripture, having used this name in a hidden way, appears with much and divine emphasis [to speak] about him, because of [his] announcing in the economy, as Son, Word, the paternal will. For it did not say by name, as it is wont to say: Michael, Gabriel, or so-and-so.' What then out of all our arguments could anyone reasonably accuse? And what could he blame in the faith of the orthodox, which from nowhere has [ground] to be called to account? And how [is it] not worthy to believe that the Holy Spirit gives revelation royally, or divinely, but the angels liturgically, or serving-wise? As [it is] hard, then, as he says, to hold to the tillers [for one] to whom [skill] of steering is not present, so [it is] hard also to teach [for one] to whom the grace of the divine Spirit, which works the salvation of men with the Father and the Son, is not present, nor is it [his] to know the certainty found also in the riddles of the oracles and the answer given from the knowledge of faithful men, and [for one] to whom without a contentious and contradicting and varied purpose there is no utterance of speech. And I know clearly, O well-reputed angels of God who dwell in the heavenly light, that you, as blameless and perfect, were not vexed at the things said by me, on account of the angels like you according to nature, not according to the praiseworthiness of the will; on whom blame followed from the beginning, as also [they] who appear to you most of all as some unpersuasive [ones] toward the contest against the truth. For the discourse for me is on behalf of the divine Spirit who enlightens all things and lavishes on the creatures the divine things matching [those] of the Father and of his Only-begotten, who sanctified you too and is glorified together by you with the Father and the Son through the thrice-holy praise. Rather you also nodded assent to me when I acclaimed this Spirit of the hypostasis of God one and only and God; and you would perhaps wish (and the book keeps festival for me in this part) through excess of your goodwill toward the venerable and consubstantial Trinity both that the words spoken from the sense of the Scriptures by many and now by me were yours, and that silence never be laid upon them, and that all men spend the leisure from their affairs on such a subject. Therefore for this reason, by the most high judgment, you, O holy Michael, were appointed to rule the [page number 76, debris] bodiless hosts and were honoured with a girdle, as it were, of the mind, and you are a certain fragrance of the all-holy and compassionate Trinity ruling all; and you, O holy Gabriel, were chosen to serve the mystery of the unspeakable economy, as one who holds his tongue and faithful; and one with one, another with another, not even having asked, has been honoured with a God-given gift, such as others too [have] not, and such as we too [have] not; but we too [with one] such as you too [have] not. For God the Word, not for the sake of the angels who sinned [became] an angel, but for the sake of the men in sin a man, unchangeably, unconfusedly, sinlessly, ineffably, as he knows and willed, from the Virgin and according to her flesh and [that] of all of us he became, remaining what he was and is and will be, one and the same. 'For one,' he says, 'holy, one Lord Jesus Christ to the glory of God the Father.' And thus, as from earth to heavens he went up, he will come the second time, angelic glorious phalanxes, myriads of myriads, ministering to him, and further he will both judge and act according to his love of mankind. Therefore after the churches houses of prayer to God named with your appellation, O well-pleasing pair of archangels, not in the cities alone, but also in lanes privately and houses and fields were founded, adorned with gold and silver or even ivory; and men go even to the places farther from the [land] that bore them, which have the houses of prayer put forward as, so to speak, halls of attainments, not shrinking from crossing a sea too, if need be, a long [one], and a road of many successive days [continues in the next section] ...
pass_b_english: …things to come, or what sovereign right to give revelation, can they have, as God has? These angels do not know things of themselves, nor do they give revelation by any authority of their own; the fact proves itself even without any argument. If, then, because the one word alone is said of both in common, you have sounded the call to blame and accusation, you have acted rashly and without thought, and not even to the point. For even if some others should happen to say of God the Father that he gives revelation and that he is good, it would not be fitting for us to say the opposite.

Let me tell you something else as well: “Consider whether, by the angel who gave revelation to the centurion, Scripture did not mean the Saviour, the Holy of Holies. For in using this name Scripture appears to speak of him in a hidden way, with great and divine emphasis, because as Son and Word he announced the Father’s will in the plan of salvation. For it did not name him, as it usually does: Michael, Gabriel, or so-and-so.”

What, then, in all our arguments could anyone reasonably charge? And what fault could he find with the faith of the orthodox, which gives no ground anywhere for being called to account? And how is it not right to believe that the Holy Spirit gives revelation royally, that is, as God does, while the angels do so as ministers, that is, as servants? As it is hard, then, as the saying goes, to hold the tiller for one who has no skill in steering, so it is hard also to teach for one to whom the grace of the divine Spirit is not present, the grace that works the salvation of men together with the Father and the Son; for one who does not know the certainty that is found even in the riddles of the sacred oracles, nor the answer given from the understanding of faithful men; and for one whose speech never comes out without a contentious, contradicting and shifting intent.

But I know clearly, O glorious angels of God, who dwell in the heavenly light, that you, being blameless and perfect, were not offended at what I have said about the angels who are like you in nature, though not in the praiseworthiness of their will. Blame has followed them from the beginning, and they seem to you, above all, to be unpersuasive in their struggle against the truth. For my discourse is on behalf of the divine Spirit, who enlightens all things and lavishes on creatures divine gifts that rival those of the Father and his Only-begotten; who sanctified you too, and is glorified by you together with the Father and the Son in the thrice-holy hymn. Better still, you nodded your assent with me when I acclaimed this Spirit of the hypostasis of God as one and only, and as God.

And you would perhaps wish (and in this part my book keeps festival for me), out of the abundance of your goodwill toward the venerable and consubstantial Trinity, that the words spoken from the meaning of the Scriptures by many, and now by me, were your own, that silence might never be laid upon them, and that all men would spend the leisure their affairs leave them on such a subject.

Therefore, for this reason, by the most high judgment, you, holy Michael, were appointed to command the bodiless hosts, and were honoured with a girdle, as it were, of the mind, and you are a kind of fragrance of the all-holy and compassionate Trinity that is Lord of all. And you, holy Gabriel, were chosen to serve the mystery of the plan of salvation that cannot be told, as one who keeps a secret and is faithful. One has been honoured with one God-given gift and another with another, without even asking for it: a gift such as others do not have, and such as we do not have. But we too have a gift such as you do not have.

For God the Word did not become an angel for the sake of the angels who sinned, but a man for the sake of men in sin: without change, without confusion, without sin, beyond telling, as he knows and as he willed, from the Virgin, and in accordance with her flesh and that of all of us; remaining what he was and is and will be, one and the same. “For one,” he says, “is holy, one is Lord, Jesus Christ, to the glory of God the Father” (Philippians 2:11). And just as he went up from earth into the heavens, so he will come a second time (Acts 1:11), with glorious angelic battalions, myriads upon myriads, serving him; and he will also judge, and act in accordance with his love for mankind.

That is why, after the churches, houses of prayer to God bearing your name, O well-pleasing pair of archangels, have been founded not only in the cities, but also privately in lanes, in houses and in fields, adorned with gold and silver, or even ivory. And people go even to places far from the land that bore them, places that have these houses of prayer set up as, so to speak, halls where prayers are granted. They do not shrink from crossing even a wide sea, if need be, and a road of many days on end …
notes: Khazarzar; Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify

pass the word, give the signal

choices.issue: Garbled machine draft, wrong reference, page number printed as a number of hosts
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u18): retranslated. The old English read 'the matter itself is a self-evident proof of a certain division', 'you commanded to act rashly', 'the Savior, spoke [of the centurion]', 'to be a shouter' (οἰάκων ἔχεσθαι, hold the tiller), 'Just as for one who is not above governing', 'You are family', 'having not spoken aloud of Him to me', 'the Septenary' (σεπτήν), 'the 76 incorporeal hosts', 'One is honored by another', 'became all of us', 'not through sinful angels, but through men', 'the second [coming] shall come' and 'pleasant places' (εὐκτήρια, houses of prayer). Reference (1 Cor 8:6) replaced by Philippians 2:11; Acts 1:11 added. Brackets [of the centurion], [Son], [coming] removed; 'unto' removed.

choices.english: …things to come
choices.why: The sentence began in the previous section ('what innate knowledge of the …'); only the words this section holds are translated, opened with '…'.

choices.english: These angels do not know ... If, then, because the one word alone is said of both in common ... you have acted rashly
choices.why: One long conditional period broken into sentences; the first condition is granted as fact ('the fact proves itself'), the second carries the charge.

choices.term: διὰ τὸ τὴν λέξιν μόνην κατὰ κοινοῦ κατηγορεῖσθαι
choices.english: because the one word alone is said of both in common
choices.why: Logical sense of κατηγορεῖσθαι (to be predicated): the word 'give revelation' is used of the Spirit and of angels, which does not make their natures one.

choices.english: you have sounded the call to blame and accusation
choices.why: παραγγέλλω, to pass the word of command; the opponents rally to censure.

choices.english: “Consider whether ... or so-and-so.”
choices.why: The copy-text sets this argument in quotation marks although it is not Scripture; the marks are kept. Didymus offers it as a further point: the unnamed 'holy angel' of Acts 10:22 may be the Son, the messenger of the Father's will. Flagged in problems.

choices.english: the Holy of Holies
choices.why: A title of Christ; kept as a title.

choices.english: as Son and Word
choices.why: Two titles in apposition without a conjunction; 'and' joins them in English.

choices.term: βασιλικῶς ἤτοι θεϊκῶς ... λειτουργικῶς ἤγουν διακονικῶς
choices.english: royally, that is, as God does ... as ministers, that is, as servants
choices.why: Each pair is a word and its gloss; ἤτοι and ἤγουν mean 'that is'.

choices.term: ὡς χαλεπὸν οὖν, καθά φησιν, οἰάκων ἔχεσθαι. ὅτῳ κυβερνητικῆς οὐχ ὕπεστιν
choices.english: As it is hard, then, as the saying goes, to hold the tiller for one who has no skill in steering
choices.why: The full stop after ἔχεσθαι in the copy-text splits one comparison (ὡς ... οὕτω); read as one sentence. καθά φησιν introduces a proverb, rendered 'as the saying goes'.

choices.english: the riddles of the sacred oracles
choices.why: τὰ λόγια are the Scriptures; 'sacred' marks that in English.

choices.term: οἷς ἐξ ἀρχῆς μέμψις παρηκολούθησεν, ὡς καὶ οἵτινες ὑμῖν μάλιστα ἀπίθανοί τινες ... φαίνονται
choices.english: Blame has followed them from the beginning, and they seem to you, above all, to be unpersuasive in their struggle against the truth
choices.why: Read as both clauses describing the fallen angels; the second could also refer to the heretics. Flagged in problems.

choices.term: φιλοτιμουμένου τὰ θεϊκὰ τοῖς κτίσμασι ... ἐφάμιλλα
choices.english: lavishes on creatures divine gifts that rival those of the Father and his Only-begotten
choices.why: φιλοτιμέομαι with an accusative, to bestow generously; ἐφάμιλλα, matching, makes the Spirit's gifts equal to the Father's and the Son's.

choices.term: πανηγυρίζει δέ μοι ἐν τῷ μέρει τούτῳ τὸ βιβλίον
choices.english: (and in this part my book keeps festival for me)
choices.why: A parenthesis inside the sentence about the angels' wish; kept in parentheses.

choices.english: venerable
choices.why: σεπτός, revered; the old 'Septenary' took it as a number.

choices.english: a girdle, as it were, of the mind
choices.why: νοερός, intellectual or spiritual; the girdle is the badge of a commander, given to a bodiless being.

choices.english: the bodiless hosts
choices.why: 76 is a printed page number in the copy-text, skipped; the old 'the 76 incorporeal hosts' printed it as a count.

choices.english: one who keeps a secret
choices.why: Literally 'holding his tongue'; fitting for the bearer of the hidden mystery of the Incarnation.

choices.term: ἄλλος δὲ ἄλλῳ ... θεοσδότῳ χαρίσματι τετίμηται
choices.english: One has been honoured with one God-given gift and another with another
choices.why: Distributive ἄλλος ἄλλῳ; the old 'One is honored by another' misread it.

choices.term: κατὰ τὴν σάρκα αὐτῆς καὶ πάντων ἡμῶν
choices.english: in accordance with her flesh and that of all of us
choices.why: He took flesh like hers and ours; the old 'became all of us' misread the genitive.

choices.term: «εἷς ... ἅγιος, εἷς κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ πατρός»
choices.english: “For one,” he says, “is holy, one is Lord, Jesus Christ, to the glory of God the Father” (Philippians 2:11)
choices.why: The words follow the liturgical acclamation 'One is holy, one is Lord' joined to Philippians 2:11, 'Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father'; Philippians 2:11 is the verse whose words are quoted. The old (1 Cor 8:6) has 'one Lord Jesus Christ' but not 'to the glory of God the Father'.

choices.term: οὕτως, ὡς ... ἀνέβη, ἥξει τὸ δεύτερον
choices.english: just as he went up ... so he will come a second time (Acts 1:11)
choices.why: Clear allusion to Acts 1:11, 'will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven'.

choices.english: battalions
choices.why: Military ranks of angels; 'phalanxes' would sound technical in English.

choices.english: halls where prayers are granted
choices.why: Literally 'town halls of attainments'; the shrines are places where people obtain what they ask, hence 'so to speak'.

choices.english: the land that bore them
choices.why: Their homeland.

choices.english: a road of many days on end …
choices.why: The sentence runs into the next section (ἔσθ' ὅτε καὶ ἀργαλέαν ἐξανῦσαι, 'sometimes even a hard one, to complete'); only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'.
